value.body:
With `scheduler.tests` on, `cargo nextest run` now runs each test under the machine-wide scheduler, and nextest's `-j` no longer caps the build. This release also fixes several causes of cache misses and bypasses: explicit linkers, `-L native` directories, and build scripts that declare `OUT_DIR`. Workspace `staticlib`/`cdylib` libraries now compile incrementally, and `HOST_CC` no longer changes between a symlinked `mbx` and its real path.

## Added

- **`cargo nextest run` tests are scheduled in the shared pool** ([#684](https://github.com/jdx/mr-boxington/pull/684), @jbellis). Before, only compilers and `cargo test` binaries waited for permits. So several agents on one machine could each start a full nextest run at once and run out of memory. With `scheduler.tests = true` (or `MBX_SCHEDULER_TESTS=1`), each nextest test process now waits for permits from the same machine-wide pool as compilers:

  ```sh
  MBX_SCHEDULER_TESTS=1 mbx nextest run --workspace
  # or, for every run:
  mbx settings set scheduler.tests true
  ```

  - mbx installs its runner through `CARGO_TARGET_<TRIPLE>_RUNNER`. Any runner you configured is still called. Cargo aliases such as `[alias] nt = "nextest run"` are scheduled too.
  - mbx records each test's CPU and peak memory under `<cache>/scheduler/tests/` and uses them to size its permit request. A test with no history asks for 1 core and 2 permits of memory. `mbx gc` removes history that hasn't been used for 30 days.
  - Listing tests never waits.
  - **Timeouts:** nextest starts a test's `slow-timeout` clock, including `terminate-after`, when it starts the runner, so time spent waiting for a permit counts as test time. After a one-second wait, mbx writes a note to the test's stderr. If your profiles set `terminate-after`, leave room for queueing.
  - These are still not scheduled: test binaries run directly, doctests, `--no-run`, commands with `--config`, `+toolchain` or `-C`, and `--archive-file` runs built for a triple that is neither the requested target nor the host.

- **The `mbx doctor` archives check falls back to `llvm-ar` and `llvm-ranlib`** when `ar` or `ranlib` isn't on `PATH`, for example on Windows ([#699](https://github.com/jdx/mr-boxington/pull/699), @Veykril). Each tool falls back separately. If a tool runs but fails, mbx reports that error instead of trying the fallback. This changes only the host probe. It doesn't change which archiver build scripts use.

## Fixed

- **`mbx nextest run -j N` no longer limits the build to N compiler permits** ([#685](https://github.com/jdx/mr-boxington/pull/685), @jbellis). For nextest, `-j`, `--jobs` and `--test-threads` set how many tests run at once, so mbx now ignores them as build limits. It reads `--build-jobs N` instead, and still falls back to `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS`. This also works through Cargo aliases. Alias expansion no longer runs `cargo --list`, which saves one Cargo subprocess per external command.
- **Setting an explicit linker no longer makes rlib and `cargo check` compilations skip the cache** ([#694](https://github.com/jdx/mr-boxington/pull/694), @jdx). A target `linker = "clang"` (for example, with `-C link-arg=-fuse-ld=mold`) made every library and check compilation report `unknown-codegen-option`, even though they never link. These compilations are now cached, and the linker is still part of the cache key. Outputs that actually link keep their existing restrictions.
- **`-L native=` directories no longer cause misses across checkouts or target dirs** ([#692](https://github.com/jdx/mr-boxington/pull/692), @jdx). Build scripts such as `libz-sys` and `aws-lc-sys` leave files there that the linker never reads but that contain the absolute target path. mbx now skips `pkgconfig/`, `cmake/` and `*.dSYM/` directories, plus `.pc`, `.cmake` and C/C++ header files, when hashing these directories. Libraries are still hashed.
- **A `-L native=` directory passed more than once now counts once against the 2 GiB native input limit** ([#691](https://github.com/jdx/mr-boxington/pull/691), @jdx). A build script that printed the same `rustc-link-search` line twice could double a 1.2 GiB directory past the limit, so the result wasn't stored (`rustc search path kind is not cacheable yet: native`). A directory nested inside another `-L native=` directory is also counted once now.
- **Crates whose build script declares `rerun-if-env-changed=OUT_DIR` build again** ([#700](https://github.com/jdx/mr-boxington/pull/700), @jdx). This is what `build-rs` emits for `build_rs::input::out_dir()`. Crates that included generated sources from `OUT_DIR` failed with `compilation result was discarded: build-script inputs changed during compilation`. They now build and are cached, and two checkouts of the same project share the cache entry.
- **Workspace libraries with a `staticlib`, `cdylib` or `dylib` crate type now compile incrementally** ([#695](https://github.com/jdx/mr-boxington/pull/695), @jdx). mbx doesn't cache these libraries, such as Tauri's `["staticlib", "cdylib", "rlib"]` template, and until now it also rebuilt them from scratch on every edit. They now get learned incremental state on the first build and reuse it after that. They're still reported as `unsupported-crate-type` bypasses. `learned_incremental = false` (`MBX_LEARNED_INCREMENTAL=0`), `MBX_VERIFY`, or a user-set `-Cincremental` turns this off.
- **Running `mbx` through a symlink and through its real path now gives the same `HOST_CC`** ([#693](https://github.com/jdx/mr-boxington/pull/693), @jdx). Before, the two paths used different C/C++ shim directories. So switching between `mbx build` and plain `cargo` (through the cargo shim) in the same target dir reran every build script that watches `HOST_CC`. Upgrading in place at the same real path still keeps the same shim directory. If you reach versioned installs through a moving `latest` symlink, each release now gets its own shim directory, so cc-based build scripts rerun once after each upgrade.

## New Contributors

* @Veykril made their first contribution in [#699](https://github.com/jdx/mr-boxington/pull/699)

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/jdx/mr-boxington/compare/v1.23.0...v1.24.0

value.body:
In a new worktree, the first `cargo check`, `cargo clippy`, or rust-analyzer check now copies dependency units from another checkout instead of starting cold. `mbx clean --under` cleans every workspace below a directory, and `mbx edit` opens the global config. This release also fixes two cases where the cache could restore stale output, and two scheduler problems that made builds wait for capacity they didn't need.

## Added

- **First checks in a new checkout start from another checkout's dependency units** ([#644](https://github.com/jdx/mr-boxington/pull/644), @jdx). Before, seeding applied only to `cargo build`. Now it also covers the [check lane](https://mr-boxington.jdx.dev/managed-targets (`target/check`) used by `check` and `clippy`, and editor checks under `target/rust-analyzer`. This helps most with git worktrees and coding agents, which usually run `cargo check` first. Each lane is seeded only from the same lane in the most recently used other checkout that has one.

  ```text
  $ git worktree add ../task-2 && cd ../task-2
  $ cargo check --workspace
  mbx[target]: copied 303 registry build units from /home/me/src/task-1
  ```

  The existing seeding rules still apply: only registry and Git dependencies are copied, Cargo 1.100 or later is required, and `target.seed = false` (`MBX_TARGET_SEED=0`) turns seeding off.

- **`mbx clean --under <ROOT>`** removes the managed target and learned incremental state of every recorded workspace at or below `ROOT`, including nested worktrees ([#668](https://github.com/jdx/mr-boxington/pull/668), @jbellis). This is for tools that delete whole checkouts and would otherwise leave nested worktrees' targets until `target.max_age` expires.
  - `ROOT` must be absolute and can't be a filesystem root. It doesn't need to exist anymore. Paths match on whole components, so `/workspace/abc` doesn't match `/workspace/abcd`.
  - Cargo isn't invoked, and `.mbx.toml` policies are skipped. The option can't be combined with a positional workspace.
  - Workspaces are cleaned in parallel, up to 8 at once. A workspace held by a running command is kept with a warning. The exit status is non-zero only if a removal fails, and mbx still tries to remove the other workspaces.

- **`mbx edit` opens the global configuration file** in `$VISUAL`, then `$EDITOR`, and falls back to `nano` (or `notepad` on Windows) ([#665](https://github.com/jdx/mr-boxington/pull/665), @jdx, based on #404 by @Kemperino). If the file doesn't exist, mbx creates it first. The command runs before the config is loaded, so you can use it to fix invalid TOML. Editor values can include arguments and quoted paths, such as `EDITOR="code --wait"`.

- **Nix flake** ([#649](https://github.com/jdx/mr-boxington/pull/649), @theduke). The repository now provides `mbx` as a flake package and app for x86-64 and ARM64 on Linux and macOS. To run it without installing:

  ```sh
  nix run github:jdx/mr-boxington -- build
  ```

  In a dev shell, put the package's Cargo wrapper first on `PATH` so that plain `cargo` commands go through mbx:

  ```nix
  shellHook = ''
    export PATH="${mbx.packages.${system}.mbx}/libexec/mbx:$PATH"
  '';
  ```

  The installation docs have a complete dev-shell example.

## Fixed

### Cache correctness

- **Changes to build-script inputs now trigger a recompile of the package's Rust crates** ([#667](https://github.com/jdx/mr-boxington/pull/667), @jdx). This includes files that a proc macro reads but rustc's dep-info doesn't list. Before, a crate using `rust-embed` with `cargo::rerun-if-changed=../dist` could get an old cached list of embedded files after files were added to `dist/`. Now the files, directory contents, symlinks, and environment variables named in `rerun-if-changed` and `rerun-if-env-changed` are part of the compilation's cache key. Packages with no `rerun-if` directives use Cargo's implicit package inputs. Unchanged inputs can still be shared across checkouts. A watched path that overlaps compiler outputs, such as `rerun-if-changed=.` with the target directory inside the package, now skips the cache for that compilation. These bypasses are reported as `build-script-input-overlaps-outputs`.
- **A file changed twice within one filesystem timestamp tick is now rehashed** ([#674](https://github.com/jdx/mr-boxington/pull/674), @jdx). Before, if a file was written, hashed, and written again within one tick, its size and timestamps stayed the same, so mbx could reuse the old digest. A cache key could then be computed from contents that were no longer on disk. Now mbx doesn't save a digest for reuse if the file was modified within the last 20 ms, or the last 2 s on filesystems that store whole-second timestamps.

### Cache coverage

- **Builds that pass `-Zuse-sync-unwind=yes` or `=no` to rustc are now cached** ([#655](https://github.com/jdx/mr-boxington/pull/655), @jdalton). The value is part of the cache key, so `yes` and `no` builds are stored separately.

### Scheduler

- **A release LTO link no longer slows dev links of the same binary** ([#670](https://github.com/jdx/mr-boxington/pull/670), @jdx). The memory scheduler recorded peak link memory by crate name only and never lowers a recorded peak. As a result, one `lto = true`, `codegen-units = 1` release link could make every later dev link reserve memory it didn't need and wait for it. Link peaks are now recorded separately for each combination of `opt-level`, `lto`, `codegen-units`, and debuginfo. Older link entries in `memory.json` are no longer read, so each profile learns its peak again on its next link.
- **Test suites that finish in under a second no longer request half the compiler pool on every run** ([#661](https://github.com/jdx/mr-boxington/pull/661), @jdx). With `scheduler.tests = true`, a suite was measured only after a complete run of at least a second. Fast suites therefore kept the never-measured default and could wait behind memory-heavy compiles. In one reported case, a 41 s step took 340–390 s. Now a complete, unfiltered run under a second is recorded as one core. Windows is unchanged because mbx can't measure CPU time there.

## Upgrade notes

Expect some cache misses on the first builds after upgrading. Rust compilations of packages with build scripts now have different cache keys ([#667](https://github.com/jdx/mr-boxington/pull/667)). Also, file digests saved by earlier versions are discarded, so files are hashed once more ([#674](https://github.com/jdx/mr-boxington/pull/674)).

## New Contributors

* @theduke made their first contribution in [#649](https://github.com/jdx/mr-boxington/pull/649)
* @jdalton made their first contribution in [#655](https://github.com/jdx/mr-boxington/pull/655)

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/jdx/mr-boxington/compare/v1.22.0...v1.23.0
